assessment: Three of the ten answer an axis the diagnosis names as a weakness. Soul-Guide Lantern is the only pick here that raises the measured breadth count, and Deflecting Swat plus Champion's Helm are the protection budget. The other seven are engine depth ranked by what improves the median game before the ceiling, per the corpus on storm math — "Separate ceiling from median: the full storm kill is the ceiling; the median game is the value engine under it — pace for the median, hold the ceiling as opportunism." Two famous cards are off the list on an oracle read: Lightning Greaves grants shroud, which stops your own Crimson Wisps from targeting Zada, and Repercussion turns Blasphemous Act's 13 damage into 13 per your own 1/1 aimed at your face.

ten.card: Birgi, God of Storytelling // Harnfel, Horn of Bounty
ten.why: Every spell you cast refunds {R} and the mana survives the step change, so a turn-5 chain of Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command and Grapeshot pays for its own fourth spell without drawing one of the four rituals.
ten.unlocks: A ritual that stays on the battlefield: the storm target's mana half stops being four one-shot cards. Harnfel, Horn of Bounty is the other face when the board is already wide and the hand is not. Throne of Eldraine is the slot — five mana for four mana that can only be spent on monocoloured spells, against three mana that pays on every cast.

ten.why: Stack 002 records Empty the Warrens as the fourth spell of the turn and eight Goblin tokens entering; through Purphoros that is 2 damage each per opponent against Impact Tremors' 1, and with devotion under five he is an indestructible enchantment your own Blasphemous Act cannot kill.
ten.unlocks: A second token-to-damage converter that needs no Goblin to die and survives the wrath that clears the swarm. Boggart Shenanigans is the slot: it is the sixth card converting a Goblin death into damage and the only one that cannot point at a creature — the corpus on what to cut, "cut duplicated function before any uncovered class".

ten.why: Graveyard is the one permanent class no card in the 99 touches; one mana on turn one exiles a card on entry, and against a table with no graveyard seat it cashes out for {1} and a card instead of rotting in hand.
ten.unlocks: Class coverage — the measured breadth count goes from two answered classes to three, per the corpus on interaction suites: "Breadth before depth: three opponents mean every permanent type appears, so cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any". Quest for the Goblin Lord is the slot: a one-mana enchantment that does nothing at all until it holds five quest counters.

ten.why: Two mana stacks the top of the library with any number of Goblins in the order you choose, and Conspicuous Snoop casts them off the top and borrows the activated ability of whichever one is showing — leave Krenko, Mob Boss on top and Snoop taps for tokens.
ten.unlocks: A tutor that is itself a Goblin: Warchief hastes it, Chieftain pumps it, Skirk Prospector eats it and Brightstone Ritual counts it. Moggcatcher is the slot — seven mana across two turns for one Goblin permanent, on a Human Mercenary that every Goblin anthem in the deck reads past. The tutor count does not move.

ten.why: Mana Geyser, Seething Song, Ruby Medallion and Storm-Kiln Artist are all already sleeved, so one card sits at the end of three separate infinite-flagged lines — and off-combo, buyback-copying Mana Geyser on the pivot turn is the biggest single mana swing the deck can make.
ten.unlocks: Copies a ritual or a payoff mid-chain and returns to hand for {3}, so the same card raises the storm count twice. All three lines are candidates until a stack scenario settles them.

ten.why: With Zada on the battlefield you take both modes — {R} for each card in an opponent's hand plus three cards off the top playable this turn — and Ruby Medallion brings it down to {1}{R}, which is a turn-4 Empty the Warrens against a table still on three lands.
ten.unlocks: Ritual and fuel in one card, the shape the storm turn is short of. It is a Game Changer: the computed floor does not move, but the pilot should know it deepens the tier-4 read. Daring Discovery is the slot — five mana, and its "up to three target creatures" does not target only one creature you control, so neither Zada nor Frontline Heroism copies it.

ten.why: Held for the turn you tap out to storm, it moves an opponent's removal spell off Zada or repoints their tutor trigger — and while you control Zada it costs no mana, which is exactly the turn you have none spare.
ten.unlocks: The single-use half of the commander-insurance taxonomy — "single-use instants (cost held mana all game but protect at the decisive moment and can cover the board)" — and the protection count goes from 2 to 3 without spending a permanent slot. Note the free cast needs Zada on the battlefield; from the command zone it is a {2}{R} instant.

ten.why: It grants hexproof rather than shroud, so your own Crimson Wisps can still target the equipped Zada — which is why Lightning Greaves, cheaper and equip {0}, is the wrong equipment for a deck whose plan is targeting its own commander.
ten.unlocks: Constant protection for the copy hub at equip {1}, and it re-arms onto Krenko, Mob Boss, Grenzo, Havoc Raiser, General Kreat or Pashalik Mons — every one of them legendary. Taken with Deflecting Swat the protection count reads 4.

ten.why: Equipped Krenko untaps whenever a creature dies and Goblin Bombardment sacrifices for free, so the untap loop asks nothing of the command zone — where stack 004 found the popular Krenko line does, and terminates for this 99 because Zada is the commander.
ten.unlocks: A free-sacrifice untap engine on two cards already in the deck. Price it honestly: Krenko is a Warrior, so equip is {4} and the investment is six mana before the first untap. All three lines need a stack scenario.

ten.why: One red mana targeting a single creature is the cheapest payload Zada copies, and buyback {3} means the same card raises the storm count on every turn you can pay for it — a five-body board turns it into +3/+0 across the team for {R}.
ten.unlocks: A recurring Zada payload that Frontline Heroism also copies, and with Storm-Kiln Artist every copy mints a Treasure. Whether that pays for its own buyback is the question a stack scenario has to settle before the line is anything but a candidate.

gaps: The synergy graph carries a shortlist for nine of these ten cards and none of those shortlists names a card in this 99 — the one exception is Jeska's Will, whose shortlist includes Ruby Medallion and Blasphemous Act. Evidence here therefore rests on combo_details and oracle text, not on the synergy channel.

The obsolescence index lists none of these ten as a replacement for a deck card. Its entries for this deck point at cards whose specific text the deck is paid on — the index is format-agnostic and cannot know which side of a trigger you are on.
Reiterate's three lines, Thornbite Staff's three and Seething Anger's one are all candidates. Seven combo claims, zero verifications: /resolve-stack is what turns any of them into evidence.

How many protection slots to buy is unsettled. strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density asks for 5-7; strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite budgets "2-4 protection generic", under which 2 is already inside the band. One of the three engine targets is commander-gated and Deflecting Swat's free cast needs Zada on the battlefield, so the answer depends on what removal these tables actually run — a deck_recon pass would settle it.

Mana Echoes and Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker both sit on in-deck combo lines and neither earned a slot: Mana Echoes is four mana that wants a board it does not build, and Kiki-Jiki's line with Conspicuous Snoop needs a third card to arrange the top of the library. If the pilot wants a twelfth and thirteenth card to watch, those are the two.
